item.title: Your agent didn’t hallucinate; it exceeded its authority
item.description: Content filters can block unsafe output. They cannot tell you whether an agent was authorized to issue that refund, touch that production system, or commit the company to an external action. Those are different problems, and most enterprises are only solving the first one.An AI agent can follow its instructions perfectly and still take an action the business never sanctioned.In commerce environments, I have seen this pattern emerge in practical ways. A service workflow calculates the correct refund amount but lacks a boundary preventing credits above what the business approved for autonomous a...

item.title: Reimagined work will create AI transformation
item.description: Organizations should approach AI less as a technology deployment and more as an opportunity to rethink how work gets done. As organizations race to adopt AI, many leaders are asking the wrong question. Too many are using AI to optimize yesterday’s workflows instead of asking a harder question: should this process still exist? Using AI in small, incremental ways—like summarizing emails or automating tasks—may create some efficiency, but it rarely creates meaningful impact....

item.title: Dating apps could help smokers quit
item.description: As cigarette imagery creeps back into pop culture, dating apps have a chance to turn swipe-based judgment into a nudge toward healthier choices—and bigger dating pools. Profile details tied to healthy living also shape many first impressions. But what if the swipe economy could also reshape public health while expanding personal connections?...
